full_judgment: 49. Regarding the submission of the learned Counsel for the appellants that since Abul Hossain were not examined an adverse presumption should be drawn against the prosecution. It became clear from the evidence, mainly from the cross-examination that Abul Hossain Pagla was almost an abnormal person, who was unfit to depose before the court and so no adverse presumption should be drawn for non-examination of Abul Hossain. The next point raised by the learned Advocate for the appellants is that all the witnesses are the relations of the deceased and there are no independent or disinterested witnesses in this case. It appears from the evidence on record that the place of occurrence was a vacant field and there is no human habitation nearby to the place of occurrence and the nearest house from the place of occurrence belonged to the deceased and their neighbours and all the neighbours are co-related including the accused persons are also neighbours of the deceased. So, it is natural that relations will come forward and see the occurrence. Mere relationship by itself cannot be a ground for rejecting testimony of a witness, unless it is shown that the witness was biased and resorted to falsehood.
